Navbar

A logo or brand link, plus navigation aligned left or right.

A navbar has two main parts: a logo or brand link, and the navigation links. Align those links left or right. The bar itself is CSS-only. Dropdowns, tabs, and the mobile collapse menu are separate components that AutoInit() starts.

The component class is navbar on a <nav>. Put links and the brand inside nav-wrapper. The bar’s own background is secondary-container and the links use on-primary, so put a filled token such as primary on the wrapper — the navbar rule wins over a utility on the same element.

Right Aligned Links

Add the right class to the ul that contains the links.

Logo
  • Sass
  • Components
  • JavaScript
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">JavaScript</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

Left Aligned Links

Add the left class to the ul, and right to the brand if you want the logo on the other side.

Logo
  • Sass
  • Components
  • JavaScript
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo right">Logo</a>
    <ul class="left hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">JavaScript</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

Centering the logo

The logo centers itself on medium and down screens. To keep it centered at every width, add center to brand-logo. You have to keep the links from overlapping it.

Logo
  • Sass
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo center">Logo</a>
    <ul class="left hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">JavaScript</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

Active Items

Add active to the link — RoutePlate styles a.active, not the list item.

Logo
  • Sass
  • Components
  • JavaScript
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li><a class="active" href="#!">JavaScript</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

Extended Navbar with Tabs

Add nav-extended so the navbar height can grow, then put extra content such as tabs in nav-content. tabs-transparent keeps the tab bar clear against the navbar color. AutoInit() starts .tabs.

Logo menu

  • Components
  • JavaScript

  • Test 4

Test 1
Test 2
Test 3

<nav class="navbar nav-extended">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <a href="#!" data-target="mobile-demo" class="sidenav-trigger">
      <i class="material-icons">menu</i>
    </a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">JavaScript</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="nav-content primary">
    <ul class="tabs tabs-transparent">
      <li class="tab"><a href="#test1">Test 1</a></li>
      <li class="tab"><a class="active" href="#test2">Test 2</a></li>
      <li class="tab disabled"><a href="#test3">Disabled Tab</a></li>
      <li class="tab"><a href="#test4">Test 4</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

<ul class="sidenav" id="mobile-demo">
  <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
</ul>

<div id="test1">Test 1</div>
<div id="test2">Test 2</div>

Fixed Navbar

Wrap the navbar in navbar-fixed to pin it and reserve its height so content is not hidden underneath. The documentation header on this site uses that pattern. A second fixed bar on this page would sit on top of it, so the live example is the site header itself. 

<div class="navbar-fixed">
  <nav class="navbar">
    <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
      <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
      <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
        <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
        <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </nav>
</div>

Navbar Dropdown Menu

Put a dropdown-content list on the page and point a dropdown-trigger at it with data-target. AutoInit() starts every .dropdown-trigger.

  • one
  • two
  • three
Logo
  • Sass
  • Components
  • Dropdownarrow_drop_down 
<ul id="dropdown1" class="dropdown-content">
  <li><a href="#!">one</a></li>
  <li><a href="#!">two</a></li>
  <li class="divider"></li>
  <li><a href="#!">three</a></li>
</ul>
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">Sass</a></li>
      <li><a href="#!">Components</a></li>
      <li>
        <a class="dropdown-trigger" href="#!" data-target="dropdown1">
          Dropdown<i class="material-icons right">arrow_drop_down</i>
        </a>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>

To initialize the dropdown yourself:

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('.dropdown-trigger');
  const instances = RoutePlate.Dropdown.init(elems, {
    // specify options here
  });
});
Open on hover

Dropdowns open on click by default (hover: false). Pass { hover: true } to open on hover instead.

      <li><a href="#!"><i class="material-icons">view_module</i></a></li>

Buttons

Add the usual button classes to a link in the list. Prefer a variant that contrasts with the bar — filled on a primary wrapper disappears. See Buttons for the variants.

Logo
  • Button
  • Button
<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a class="btn elevated waves-effect">Button</a></li>
      <li><a class="btn tonal waves-effect">Button</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>
Halfway FAB in Extended Navbar

Add a halfway FAB to an extended navbar. nav-content is the positioning context.

Logo
  • A link
  • A second link
  • A third link
Title add 
<nav class="navbar nav-extended">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <a href="#!" class="brand-logo">Logo</a>
    <ul class="right hide-on-med-and-down">
      <li><a href="#!">A link</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="nav-content primary">
    <span class="nav-title">Title</span>
    <a class="btn-floating btn-large halfway-fab waves-effect waves-light">
      <i class="material-icons">add</i>
    </a>
  </div>
</nav>

Search Bar

You can put a search form in the navbar.

<nav class="navbar">
  <div class="nav-wrapper primary">
    <form>
      <div class="input-field">
        <input id="search" type="search" required>
        <label for="search"><i class="material-icons">search</i></label>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</nav>

Mobile Collapse Button

Below the large breakpoint, hide-on-med-and-down hides the inline links and sidenav-trigger shows the menu icon. The trigger is hidden on large screens. Pair it with a sidenav whose id matches data-target.

    </a>

Initialization

After you add the trigger and the sidenav, initialize Sidenav (or let AutoInit() do it). Change the selector if you used different classes. 

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  const elems = document.querySelectorAll('.sidenav');
  const instances = RoutePlate.Sidenav.init(elems);
});
